A palm-sized Agent Computer can drive a hundred-billion-parameter large model as a 24/7 local desktop AI assistant, generating PPT from a single sentence. A holographic interactive personal terminal renders real-time graphics and powers a continuous-dialogue digital human. On July 18, at WAIC 2026 Zhangjiang Science Hall, Houmo Intelligent showcased multiple M50 Inside innovative AI terminals, bringing large models from the cloud to local devices and making edge intelligence easily accessible.

Large model inference is moving to the edge, making high-compute, low-power, easy-to-deploy chips essential. As large models migrate from cloud to edge, edge AI sees explosive growth, with industry widely labeling 2026 as the first year of edge AI. Products like AI PCs, intelligent service robots, and edge intelligent terminals are accelerating commercial deployment.

Current large model parameter scales continue to expand, but terminal device size, battery power, and heat dissipation have rigid limits. Constraints on compute, power, latency, and deployment have become core bottlenecks for large-scale edge deployment, making high-compute, low-power, easy-to-deploy edge AI chips an industry necessity.

Addressing these pain points, Houmo Intelligent's M50 chip, based on a compute-in-memory architecture, achieves 160 TOPS at 10W power consumption.

excerpt_i18n.en: On July 17, the 2026 World Artificial Intelligence Conference (WAIC) officially opened in Shanghai. The NetEase Youdao booth was bustling with crowds, where a desktop-level office assistant Agent product named LobsterAI attracted many visitors who stopped to experience it, eagerly waiting in line to "command" the AI to complete real tasks. A technician from Shanghai tried using LobsterAI on site to automatically connect local projects, run test scripts, and generate code review reports. We introduce Visual Concept Inference from Sets (VICIS), a task that evaluates this capability. Given a small context set of images sharing a concept and a query image, the model must generate new images that preserve the context-defined concept while remaining consistent with the query.
